name: EgoGroups
description: Social group detection, or the identification of humans involved in reciprocal interpersonal interactions (e.g., family members, friends, and customers and merchants), is a crucial component of social intelligence needed for agents transacting in the world. The few existing benchmarks for social group detection are limited by low scene diversity and reliance on third-person camera sources (e.g., surveillance footage). Consequently, these benchmarks generally lack real-world evaluation on how groups form and evolve in diverse cultural contexts and unconstrained settings.
